name: settings-det (settings shell + General/Appearance/Chat/Developer/Engines/Hardware, capture policy tab, update panel, operator + builder, unsaved-guard, fast-fail on data-dependent)
notes: Code-verified against routes/Settings.svelte + lib/settings/settingsNav.ts + settings/{General,Appearance,ChatSettings,Developer,Engines,System}.svelte + components/settings/{config/ConfigEditor,DangerZone,config/ConfigCodeArea,UnsavedChangesDialog,UnsavedChangesBadge,SettingsToggle}.svelte + components/settings/{about/AboutBlock,system/EngineList,system/HardwareCard,help/HelpBlock}.svelte + components/observability/CapturePolicyPanel.svelte.

14 nav keys from SETTINGS_NAV, in two groups: Settings (general, appearance, profile, chat, stt, model-defaults, developer, then llm, model-hub, tools, permissions, integrations until they leave the settings) and System (engines, hardware). The column is identical in both modes. About, Help and the danger zone live in General; the shortcut catalogue and plan mode in Chat; the editor of apollia.toml in its own Configuration entry after Developer, mode on only; the former System page in Hardware; the engine list with the stated versions and the diagnostic copy in Engines; the processor, memory and GPU in Hardware, whose paths, CLI, automatic install and Python interpreter are developer mode only; the capture and retention policy in the capture tab of the Observability screen, developer mode only, where the settings unsaved badge does not exist (the footer reset still restores the form).

plan-mode-default-toggle and auto-install-python-deps-toggle ARE the <button role=switch> (Toggle.svelte spreads data-testid onto it), NOT <input> wrappers. They are clicked directly; setChecked would also work, click keeps the two-way boundary explicit.

Settings > Configuration is the editor of apollia.toml, an entry of the column after Developer that exists only with the developer mode on (settingsNav.ts developerOnly, routes/settings/Configuration.svelte). The book turns the mode on, opens it, waits for the first numbered line (config-editor-gutter-1) and copies the path; it types nothing, so the seeded file is never written.

stt-trigger and stt-language-select are native <select> (Select.svelte) with static options (toggle/push-to-talk; the STT_LANGUAGES codes). Both are exercised via selectOption in the STT save branch, then saved through the unsaved dialog. The language values (de discarded, es saved) stay distinct from the one stt-det.json picks later, so each script still produces a real change.

UpdateCheckPanel (rendered once, inside General.svelte, variant bare) is an external-update boundary only when unstubbed: the first click on update-check-btn (28-update-checker-boundary) reaches the real GitHub endpoint of tauri.conf.json and lands on whatever the host's connectivity gives. Every other phase is reached by stubbing check_for_update (commands/updates.rs UpdateCheckResult: available, current_version, new_version, release_notes, channel_unavailable) after a remount (hardware then general, so the panel starts idle whatever the boundary click left). The stub imitates a backend type and drifts silently if that struct changes.
Danger cards are screenshot-only; no reset btn or confirm dialog is triggered (real resets live in destructive.json). The onboarding reset sits in Appearance now.

settings-mobile-nav-toggle / -sheet render only when sidebarState === 'drawer', i.e. under 768 px (Settings.svelte:423 `{#if isMobile}`, isMobile = $sidebarState === 'drawer' at :86; layout.ts:28/119 MD_QUERY). The narrow block after screenshot 35 resizes to 700x800 (resizeWindow lifts the 900x600 minimum), clicks the toggle (mobileOpen = true, :432), closes the Sheet with Escape on the nav (the keydown bubbles to the panel's onkeydown -> onclose, Sheet.svelte:45-49,81; the sheet renders no close testid), and restores 1280x800 before the mode chip is touched: the block holds no picker and no window.confirm.

about-copy-data-dir is asserted, not about-data-dir-unknown. They are the two arms of one #if on SystemInfo.data_dir, the runner has no either/or step, and the seeded HOME always resolves, so the unknown arm is unreachable under this harness. It stays covered by the Rust test test_system_info_reports_the_resolved_data_directory.

The three external help cards (docs, community, report) and about-link-github / about-link-report are asserted with expect/waitFor and never clicked: they hand off to the system browser, which the runner cannot come back from. help-link-shortcuts is the one card that navigates in-app, so it is the one that is clicked.

observability-toggle-debug_log_prompt is the one sensitive flag (Observability.svelte:79-81): clicking it while off opens the ConfirmDialog observability-sensitive-confirm instead of flipping (requestToggle :157-165, the {#key} nonce snaps the Toggle back). The block after 13b plays both composed buttons (ConfirmDialog.svelte:42/50): cancel leaves cfg untouched (:175-179), confirm sets debug_log_prompt = true in memory (:169-173) and dirties the explicit-save form, which settings-subpage-reset restores (handleReset :152-155) so apollia.toml is never written and the nav guard stays quiet.

observability-open-editor opens the settings window on Settings > Configuration (openSettingsWindow), where the capture policy keys live in the editor of apollia.toml; the developer mode is on on that screen, so the editor renders. No other application opens.

update-releases-link is played under stubs: check_for_update resolves channel_unavailable true, which is phase no_channel (UpdateCheckPanel.svelte:102, :164-176), and plugin:opener|open_url resolves null so the click (openExternalUrl -> openUrl, externalLink.ts:35-46) never launches the host browser. Nothing in-app changes after that click by design, so the block asserts the phase before it (update-no-channel-label, the link itself) and that the panel is untouched after it (link and update-check-btn still rendered); the stub is what keeps the click harmless, not what proves it.

help-hero-cta is played under a plugin:opener|open_url stub resolving null: the anchor's onclick is handleExternalLinkClick (HelpHero.svelte:54, externalLink.ts:98-105), which preventDefaults and hands https://docs.apollia.fr/... to the opener, so the webview stays on the help page (help-hero-cta and help-section asserted after the click). `aria-disabled` follows navigator.onLine (Help.svelte:38-50) and only removes pointer events; the runner's el.click() is programmatic, so the handler runs online or offline. No in-app state changes on that click, so the block can assert nothing beyond the page staying mounted.

shortcuts-search is a plain bind:value filter (Shortcuts.svelte:41-55, 85-92): a no-match query renders shortcuts-empty (:99-104), an empty query restores the groups; local state, nothing persisted, the page is not nav-guarded.

update-install-btn is played twice under stubs, both after a remount. Happy path: check_for_update resolves available true with new_version 99.0.0 (update-available-label contains 99.0.0, update-changelog rendered), install_update resolves null, and the phase moves downloading -> installed (UpdateCheckPanel.svelte:110-126): installed renders no testid of its own, so it is proven by the three waitGone (update-install-btn, update-download-progress, update-check-btn), the only phase reachable from runInstall that renders none of them; error would keep update-check-btn as retry. The real install_update would replace the binary and restart the app before the report lands (commands/updates.rs:172), which is why it is never let through. Error path: install_update rejects a string, humanize keeps it as detail (lib/errors/humanize.ts:251-263) and update-error-banner contains it. listen("update-download-progress") still reaches the real event plugin; nothing emits on it.

The developer mode is one switch in Settings > Developer (developer-mode-toggle, developer-mode-on, developer-mode-off), written to [desktop] developer_mode of the seeded apollia.toml; every book turns it on and off there, never per screen.

Model defaults is walked once in the first pass: its five blocks in the order of the page (images, context, guardrails, bypass, unload). The refused figure of the image field is left to Vitest: its anchor, model-defaults-image-side-error, would also resolve through the -error suffix the option rows compose, so naming it here would mask it. The policy state is played under five get_resolved_setting stubs in patch mode, one per block (llm.images.limit_side, llm.defaults.context, llm.guardrails.level, llm.guardrails.bypass, llm.residency.idle_unload_minutes): the real call runs and only the source field of its ResolvedSetting (lib/ipc/settings.ts) becomes policy, so each block shows its policy note with the value in force; the page is left and reopened because it reads its values on mount, and the stubs are cleared before the next entry.

The resource monitor and the engine table are played under stubs, because their states depend on the host. get_resource_usage (lib/ipc/system.ts ResourceUsage, VramUsage) is rejected before the first mount of System > Hardware of the boot, which is the only moment resource-monitor-measuring exists (the store keeps its last figures afterwards), then resolved with a dedicated, a unified and an unmeasured video memory in turn; the store reads every two seconds, so each waitFor allows eight. list_engines (EnginesResponse, EngineEntry, EngineVariantUpdate) resolves three llama-server builds, one embedded and in service, one downloaded with an update on the channel, one imported whose banner contradicts its tag; check_engine_updates (EngineCheckResponse) and set_engine_channel (EngineSettings) are stubbed because the real ones fetch the channel manifest over the network, and a real channel write would outlive the section. The block ends on a real list_engines (waitGone engine-row-tag-mismatch) and leaves the developer mode off. These stubs imitate backend types and drift silently if the types change.

System > Engines opens on the engine per format and filters its table. The table shows by default only the builds the host can run, so each time the page is mounted under the stubbed list the compatibility filter is set to all before a CUDA or Vulkan row is waited for (engines-filter-compat). The engine of the GGUF format is chosen under a set_setting stub (lib/ipc/settings.ts ResolvedSetting), because a real write would stay in the seeded apollia.toml and change which binary the next book starts; the removed variant is played by resolving list_engines without the Vulkan build after it was chosen (engine-format-gguf-fell-back), then the list is put back. The MLX line exists on a Mac with an Apple chip only and is left to Vitest. The automatic update is switched under the same stub, and its policy state under a get_resolved_setting stub in patch mode on engines.auto_update, the page being left and reopened because it reads its settings on mount.

Hardware, the graphics devices: the seeded Apple machine shows its single device, its switch disabled and the note that says why; `open_hardware_window` is stubbed (type HardwareWindowOutcome) so no second window opens under the runner; a three-device profile (type HardwareResponse, with its `devices`) and a policy-fixed `llm.devices.disabled` (type ResolvedSetting) are stubbed to reach the policy mention and the note of a device the engine did not list, then cleared. The diagnostic copy of Engines is gone: its facts are copied by `hardware-copy-info`.

Settings > Developer, mode on: the Engines block carries the engine channel and the automatic update System > Engines shows too (developer-engine-channel-select, developer-engine-auto-update) and the automatic purge; Experimental carries the debugging blocks, the consumption widget and the load settings in presets. Turning developer-resource-widget-switch on writes [desktop] resource_widget of the seeded apollia.toml and mounts sidebar-resource-widget at the foot of the sidebar; a click on it opens System > Hardware on the resource monitor. The book turns the switch back off before it leaves the page, so the later sections render the sidebar without the widget.

Appearance, the display choices: the navigation position, the view mode and the generation info are native <select> played with selectOption and set back to their default; the two scroll switches and the reasoning vignette are <button role=switch> set off then on with setChecked; the message style is a radiogroup whose two buttons are clicked, blocks then bubbles. Every choice is left on its default, since it is kept in the browser storage of the seeded home and the books that follow read the chat in bubbles with the navigation on the left. What a choice does to the chat (plain text, the line under the last answer, the scroll on send, the fade of a live thought) is held by Vitest; this book only proves each control exists and answers.
